subsystems.name: Reprogramming payload
subsystems.role: the genes or molecules that reset a cell's epigenetic state.

subsystems.name: Delivery vehicle
subsystems.role: gets the payload into the right cells and no others.
parts: engineered AAV capsids or lipid nanoparticles

subsystems.name: Senescent-cell clearance
subsystems.role: removes 'zombie' cells that secrete inflammatory signals and drive tissue ageing.
parts: senolytic small molecules (e.g. BCL-2 family inhibitors)

subsystems.name: Safety and control circuitry
subsystems.role: keeps partial reprogramming from tipping into uncontrolled growth.

subsystems.name: Age measurement and biomarkers
subsystems.role: tells whether the treatment actually worked.

buildSteps.title: Measure biological age first
buildSteps.detail: Blood and tissue samples are run through epigenetic clocks so a baseline exists before any treatment.

buildSteps.title: Design the payload
buildSteps.detail: Genes for the reprogramming factors are codon-optimised, and c-Myc is usually left out because of its cancer risk; a drug-responsive promoter is attached so expression can be switched on and off.

buildSteps.title: Choose the delivery route
buildSteps.detail: The payload is packaged in a viral vector or lipid nanoparticle whose surface is chosen to reach one target tissue, with a promoter that only fires in those cells.

buildSteps.title: Test in human cells and organoids
buildSteps.detail: Cells in culture are given short pulses of the factors; the goal is a younger methylation pattern and better function while the cell keeps its identity.

buildSteps.title: Animal studies
buildSteps.detail: Mice with a switchable reprogramming gene are treated in cycles and monitored for lifespan, organ function and tumour formation.

buildSteps.title: Add senolytic clearance
buildSteps.detail: Senescent cells are killed or neutralised, reducing the inflammatory environment that pushes other cells back toward ageing.

buildSteps.title: Safety testing
buildSteps.detail: Long-term studies check for cancer, immune reactions to the vector and off-target editing in unintended organs.

buildSteps.title: Human trials
buildSteps.detail: Trials begin with a single enclosed tissue, such as the eye, where any abnormal growth can be contained; systemic dosing would come only after that is shown safe.

buildSteps.title: Combined, monitored regimen
buildSteps.detail: If it works, treatment becomes a repeated, dose-scheduled programme with regular clock measurements and cancer screening rather than a one-off cure.

prerequisites.why: induced pluripotent stem cells were demonstrated in 2006, and cyclic partial reprogramming extended lifespan and improved tissue function in mice.
AAV and lipid nanoparticles are used clinically, but not yet with the precision and repeat dosing a whole-body ageing treatment needs.
several are in human trials for specific diseases, but not yet shown to be safe for long-term use in healthy people.
epigenetic clocks correlate well with age, but regulators do not yet accept them as proof a treatment works.
fully reprogrammed cells form tumours; how to reprogram partially and reliably in every tissue is unsolved.

pathway.milestone: senolytics in early human trials for specific diseases; partial reprogramming only in animals
pathway.unlocks: safety data and proof that ageing markers can move in the right direction.

pathway.milestone: first human trials of reprogramming factors confined to one enclosed tissue
pathway.unlocks: evidence that the approach can be given safely to people at all.

pathway.milestone: organ-targeted systemic regimens judged by epigenetic clocks and function tests
pathway.unlocks: treatments for specific age-related conditions rather than 'ageing' in general.

pathway.milestone: combination therapies restoring several organ systems, with regulators accepting ageing-related endpoints
pathway.unlocks: a genuine extension of healthy lifespan — though the biology and the cancer risk remain the hard limits.
